headlines.label: Cold start, 32 services
headlines.method: GCE e2-standard-8, 32 services plus 32 store containers in both arms. Median of 5 trials, page cache dropped before each. Both run orders.

headlines.label: Idle memory, one service
headlines.method: OrbStack Debian 12 VM on Apple Silicon, 20 s after ready. Docker total includes dockerd, containerd and shims.

headlines.label: Failed requests during redeploy
headlines.method: 32 services, 50 clients, 15 min, both run orders. Each arm used its own redeploy method, so this is not a like-for-like swap comparison.

headlines.label: Static analysis, 32 services
headlines.method: anode inspect on the marketplace example, median of 5 runs on a Mac. Lockfile hash identical in all 20 analysis runs.

runs.title: Marketplace: anode vs Docker, 32 services
runs.machine: GCE e2-standard-8, 32 GB, Debian 12, us-central1-a, on-demand
runs.n: 2 run orders per arm; 5 cold-start trials per run; one 15-minute load run per order
rows: Daemon RSS (store containers in both arms)
loses: Services memory (cgroup): anode 526 to 533 MB vs Docker 504 to 511 MB, about 4% higher.
Redeploy comparison uses different procedures: anode deploy from the Mac vs our own batched stop, remove, rename, start script for Docker. It is not Docker's best method.
Smoke test: the same 3 PUT routes return 500 in both arms. Not investigated.
Steady-state load at 100 and 500 RPS is a tie (see the steady-state run).

runs.title: Steady state: bare unit vs anode unit vs Docker
runs.machine: GCE target VM with Caddy on port 80 (machine type not recorded in the README); load VM anode-loadgen, e2-standard-4, same zone
runs.n: 1 run per cell, 60 s measured after 10 s warm-up
loses: Service CPU at 100 RPS: anode 7.4% vs bare 4.2% and Docker 4.5%. One run each, so the gap is not established.
At 1,000 RPS all arms top out near 915 to 922 RPS. That is the load path, so this row does not separate the arms.
No direct-port arm: every arm goes through Caddy, so Caddy's own cost is not isolated.
Docker's 1,000 RPS CPU sample was discarded after the PID read failed.

runs.title: Failure matrix: SIGTERM, database outage, port taken
runs.machine: Same GCE VM as the marketplace run, 32 anode units and 32 store containers
rows: automatic after Restart=always, 3 s delay plus boot
immediate once Postgres returns; no restart
Port taken (:21059 held by another process)
bind: address already in use; restart loop about every 4 s
service down until the port is freed
automatic once the port is freed
loses: No graceful shutdown: the service exits on SIGTERM, so in-flight requests fail. This is the biggest known gap.
Not run: OOM under the 1G memory limit, crash-loop, bad migration, non-compiling deploy, full disk.
The matrix does not record the installed unit file, so the memory limit the VM ran with is unverified.

runs.title: Port collisions under anode dev
runs.machine: Local machine (not recorded in the README); 10 copies of examples/sample-shop
rows: 10 of 10 healthy, 20 distinct ports, all ready within 1.4 s
1 of 10 started; 9 failed with "port is already allocated"
loses: All copies shared one Postgres container started by hand, because anode dev asked for external DB URLs. Per-copy store isolation is not tested.
The Compose side used nginx with the same port mapping, not the sample-shop images.

runs.title: Analyzer time and single-service memory
runs.machine: Apple Silicon Mac (analysis); OrbStack Debian 12 arm64 VM (services)
runs.n: 5 runs per fixture for analysis; 20 s idle samples for memory
loses: Idle memory, one service: anode 5.5 MB vs Docker 102 to 106 MB including daemons. Docker's service process alone is 5.8 MB, so the gap is the daemon, not the service.
12 services on GCE: Docker ready in 8.9 s vs anode 10.9 s. The anode arm's extra time is mostly PostgreSQL startup and unit ordering; not profiled.
In that 12-service run, Caddy routed /healthz to a single service, so other services were not publicly reachable. It did not affect readiness numbers.
